comparison: Perfect overlap on claims C119-C123 regarding RING domain repositioning mechanism. Both evaluations agree this is speculative and lacks direct structural evidence. Strong overlap on claims C98-C105 regarding H3K9me3's role in directing ubiquitylation. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval emphasizes 'multiple lines of evidence' linking reader and writer functions; peer review accepts this as part of 'detailed biochemical and proteomic analysis.'

Strong overlap on claims C5, C23, C26-C37 regarding reciprocal positive allostery. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes 'true reciprocal allostery rather than simple additive effects'; peer review explicitly acknowledges 'reciprocal positive allostery' as a novel contribution distinguishing this work from Fang et al.

Strong overlap on claims C48-C56 regarding HeDNA-stimulated ubiquitylation activity. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes 'dramatic HeDNA-specific activation'; peer review states 'compelling evidence' and acknowledges this as a 'major novel finding' with 'sufficient novel insight.'

Strong overlap on claims C38-C45 regarding intramolecular domain interactions and DNA-induced conformational changes. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval emphasizes evidence for 'intramolecular conformational changes rather than oligomerization'; peer review accepts this as the 'mechanism for positive allostery.'

Strong overlap on claims C87-C94 regarding mass spectrometry identification of ubiquitylation sites. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes 'HeDNA-dependent enrichment' with 'appropriate MS/MS validation'; peer review acknowledges mass spectrometry work as part of comprehensive analysis supporting allosteric activation.

Strong overlap on claims C75-C86 regarding lysine prioritization and allosteric switch model. Strong overlap on claims C107-C108, C111-C112 regarding integrative model of chromatin targeting and allosteric activation. Both evaluations SUPPORT this conceptual framework. Moderate overlap on claims C3, C15-C19 regarding genetic complementation showing HeDNAmut fails to rescue despite binding. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. Moderate overlap on claims C63-C68 regarding mutational validation of domain requirements. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes 'systematic mutational analysis validates requirement for each domain'; peer review accepts these as mechanistic details supporting HeDNA-dependent activation story.

Partial overlap on claims C57-C62 regarding mononucleosome ubiquitylation and trans-acting model. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes 'reasonable inference from competition data'; peer review accepts as part of overall ubiquitylation activation mechanism.

Minimal overlap on claims C57-C58. Both evaluations SUPPORT HeDNA-dependent nucleosome ubiquitylation. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of competition experiments; peer review acknowledges as part of broader finding that HeDNA stimulates ubiquitylation activity.

Moderate overlap on claims C69-C74 regarding ruling out common E3 ligase activation mechanisms. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings. OpenEval notes data 'effectively rule out two common mechanisms'; peer review accepts as part of mechanistic characterization, though notes overall mechanism remains incompletely explained.

Partial overlap on claims C95-C97 regarding differential auto-ubiquitylation sites. Both evaluations SUPPORT these findings.
